Waitangi Day 2027: what to expect

Sample post, unofficial1/5Slide 1 of 5

Dawn service at 5am, then a free festival all day.

Dawn service at 5am, then a free festival all day. Haere mai to Waitangi Day 2027, Rā o Waitangi.

On 6 February, whānau from all communities and backgrounds gather at Waitangi to commemorate the first signing of Te Tiriti o Waitangi in 1840. The festival is free, and it starts at 5am with a dawn service in Te Whare Rūnanga.

Swipe for what to expect: all⁠-⁠day entertainment across three stages, more than 150 market stalls with art, crafts, clothing and food, and children’s activities. The Treaty Grounds buildings are closed for the day, and the full 2027 programme will be available in January.

Bring the whole whānau.

#WaitangiDay #RāoWaitangi #WaitangiTreatyGrounds #BayOfIslands #Aotearoa

TimelineUnofficial sample

How Te Tiriti was signed

Now showing:

1840

I care about telling this story accurately and with respect for Te Tiriti o Waitangi. I kept every line to what its page says.

Brief
I made a short timeline of how Te Tiriti o Waitangi was signed on 5 and 6 February 1840.
Made
I took the wording from the Waitangi Treaty Grounds website, waitangi.org.nz, and used only type and simple shapes. I left out people, taonga and copies of the document.
Why it works
It sticks to its page: a marquee on 5 February, then over 40 rangatira (chiefs) signing on 6 February.

Overview

One newsletter

A newsletter comes in, goes to one brand's system, and is checked. Tap a step to see it.

  1. Ask the brand Every email newsletter starts by naming its brand. New Image and Nutrimetics each have their own system, on one account.
  2. Own system Each newsletter goes to one brand's system only. The two brands are never mixed.
  3. Checks Brand check: footer, colours, images and terms wording are checked before upload.
  4. Approve Approval: nobody sends until a person approves. A 735⁠-⁠line program also checks every send.

Overview

Four steps

Posts are built from a list and sent to a review page. Tap a step to see what happens there.

  1. The program builds posts A program builds posts, carousels and reels from a list of the posts to make, so I do not build each by hand. It is made of 483 files.
  2. The team checks them The team checks each post on phone or desktop and leaves notes.
  3. Notes go back together The notes come back together, and the posts are fixed.
  4. Approved posts Approved posts are ready to publish. 505 review pages are active and 582 are stored.

How I work

Plan, make, publish, measure.

How I would work with you: four steps, repeated each week. What I learn goes into the next plan.

What I learn feeds the next plan

  1. Plan

    A content calendar built around Waitangi Day and the other dates your visitors plan for.

  2. Make

    Images and short video in Canva and CapCut. I write the English copy. A fluent reader checks any te reo before it is used.

  3. Publish

    Facebook, Instagram and email. I would send posts through a review app, where the team checks them and leaves notes.

  4. Measure

    Opens, saves and shares, looked at each week. I would send you a one⁠-⁠page report, and what I learn goes back into the plan.
